title: Privileged session change-lineage format and logging taxonomy for RBAC v2
creator: Rohit Menon
description:
Problem: current admin/audit logs do not capture a reliable, minimal-change lineage for privileged sessions and RBAC v2 policy mutations. We need a compact, queryable format that links SSO/SAML assertion context, operator session, and target object diffs so security teams can reconstruct intent, scope, and exact changes for compliance and forensics.

Goal: define a canonical 'change-lineage' envelope for privileged sessions that: 1) records actor identity and assertion provenance; 2) captures target references and an efficient diff/patchset for the state change; 3) supports deterministic hashing for indexing and de-duplication; 4) is resilient to redaction and sampling policies; 5) is small enough for high-throughput audit pipelines.

This ticket covers schema, taxonomy (what to log), compact diff encoding rules, SAML enrichment mapping, retention/sampling guidance, and a rollout/migration plan including dual-write and backfill strategy.
acceptance_criteria: Schema document with example payloads checked into Confluence and linked in this ticket
Encoding rules that allow deterministic reconstruction and minimal size for top-90%-frequent changes
SAML/SSO enrichment mapping documented and implementation knobs defined for service accounts vs human operators
Backward-compatible ingestion: existing audit consumers must accept new envelope with fallbacks; infra team signs off on retention impact
Canary dual-write option implemented in runtime for 2% of privileged sessions and metrics dashboard shows parity for 10k events
proposed_change_lineage_shape:
Primary envelope (human-readable example): {
  "envelope_id": "env_20250218_0001",
  "ts": "2025-02-18T18:14:32Z",
  "tenant_id": "acct_42",
  "session_id": "sess_7f3a",
  "trace_id": "trace-abc123",
  "actor": {"kind": "user", "id": "u-roland", "display_name": "Roland King", "auth_provider": "saml:acme-corp", "assertion_ref": "saml-assertion-987"},
  "actor_context": {"ip": "18.19.20.21", "user_agent": "curl/7.85"},
  "operation": "update-policy",
  "target_refs": [{"type": "rbac_policy", "id": "policy-24"}],
  "change_lineage": [ /* ordered compact patches (see rules) */ ],
  "metadata": {"ticket_link": "https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RBAC/PR-312"}
}
diff_encoding_rules: Canonical ops: add, remove, replace, move, patchset. Use JSON Pointer-like 'path' for schema addressing.
Store small constant-length hashes for 'before' values when available (format h:<hex>) to avoid logging sensitive full values while enabling equality checks.
When value replacement contains secrets or PII, emit a redaction token ("<REDACTED>") and capture structured metadata: original_type and original_length for forensic needs.
Patchset entries must be order-preserving and include an op-level sequence number to support replay and partial-apply semantics across consumers.
Binary blobs or large lists should be referenced by content-addressable blob id (cid:...) with an explicit retention class; never inline large binaries in change_lineage.
Compact wire encoding: top-level envelope is newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON). The change_lineage can be an escaped JSON string for index-friendly ingestion, or an array for full-fidelity pipelines.
Deterministic hashing: canonicalize JSON (sorted keys, normalized whitespace) before hashing. Hash algorithm: SHA256 truncated to 64-bit hex (h:<16hex>).
actor_target_resolution: Map SAML assertion to actor via 'assertion_ref' which links to the raw assertion stored in a short-lived secure store; the envelope stores assertion_ref not raw assertion unless retention policy allows.

Differentiate actor kinds: human user, service_account, scheduled_job, external_integrations. Each kind has required fields: human -> display_name + email, service_account -> service_id + owner_team, integration -> connector_id.
When operator is acting on behalf of another identity (delegation), log both 'actor' (performer) and 'requested_by' (originating principal) with their assertion_refs.

Target normalization: canonical target references use type prefixes (rbac:policy-24, project:proj-11, key:key-3). For composite targets (policy + binding), emit separate target_refs entries rather than embedding hierarchy.

Session linking: include 'session_id' and 'auth_flow' (interactive|api|bot) to distinguish UI-driven admin edits vs automated jobs. Runtime will set auth_flow based on token type or SAML authnContext.
Service account activity should capture the 'caller_chain' up to the human owner to support accountability for automated changes.
Fallback: if identity cannot be resolved to a known Redwood principal, tag actor.kind=external and populate external_identity fields (issuer, sub) when available.
Cross-tenant admin actions must include the invoking tenant in 'invoker_tenant' and the affected tenant in 'tenant_id' for audit separation.
retention_and_sampling_policy: Default retention classes: privileged_sessions (90d), admin_policy_changes (365d), high-fidelity forensics (5y) - configurable per tenant and legal hold.

Adaptive sampling: sample 100% for P0/P1 customers and high-sensitivity targets; otherwise downsample repetitive machine-driven events with deterministic reservoir sampling keyed on actor+target+patch_hash.
Redaction policy: PII elements redacted at write-time with tokens; redactable fields are enumerated in schema. Originals may be kept in encrypted forensic store with separate access controls.
Audit pipeline will add derived indexes (actor_id, target_id, op_count, patch_hash) to support fast queries without expanding full payload retention.
Retention side-effects must be surfaced in Console billing/metrics so customers can understand storage costs for extended retention classes.
rollout_plan: 1) Finalize schema and doc in Confluence (this ticket).
2) Implement writer-side dual-write: old 'admin_audit_v1' + new 'change_lineage_v2' under a feature flag. Start with 2% of privileged sessions.
3) Build ingestion compatibility layer that can accept either v1 or v2 envelopes and populate read-models.
4) Create dashboard and parity tests comparing v1->v2 for identical events (latency, size, completeness).
5) Increase canary to 25% for one week, validate, then 100% traffic. Decommission v1 after 90 days and backfill critical windows if requested by security/compliance.
6) Provide migration tool (offline) to convert historical v1 events to the v2 envelope for customers on request.
migration_steps: Schema registry entry created and versioned (change-lineage@v1).
Runtime writers add dual-write flag and recording of assertion_ref linking to secure assertion store.
Ingestion team builds a tolerant parser: accept old shape and map to minimal v2 envelope for read consumers.
Create conversion job to backfill high-priority tenants' last 12 months on-demand.
Update retention config UI and document costs for extended retention.
notes_and_decisions: Decision: do NOT store full SAML assertions inline in audit events. Use assertion_ref to a short-lived encrypted store. This reduces size and surface area for accidentally leaked assertions.

Trade-off: storing before/after values increases forensic fidelity but raises PII risk and storage costs. We've chosen hashed-before + redaction tokens for most fields and full retention only under forensic class.
We will use NDJSON for pipeline simplicity but allow array-form for downstream full-fidelity consumers behind a toggle.
Indexing: we prioritize indexing by patch_hash and actor_id rather than full payload content to reduce cold-query costs.
